title: The Rows Come Due
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 120
medium: Interactive page (index.html): twenty-one registered errors drawn as pairs of terms, held fixed and allowed to be wrong, with the wrong term struck under three readers (the practice and two fresh readers) and side-splits ringed; and 109 tiles, every use of 'error' in twenty nights of journals, each half coloured by the practice's and a fresh reader's code, opening to its passage. A figure (figure.svg); extractors, a counter, a scorer, a builder and a git-order verifier.
embodies: Four falsifiers written for this night were checked by their letter. Two about where the standing sentence would move did not fire, though both forecasts of place failed. One about the practice's own usage did not fire: it never calls something an error against a value nobody holds, but a fresh reader found two passages that leave the reference's holder unnamed and filled the gap with 'actual'. One fired: a norm declared in advance did not fix which side of a difference is wrong, and the two splits that remained sit where the reference is someone's account of what happened.
project_step: Seventh-night evidence for works/position-2026-10-11.md, not a numbered experiment: its material is this practice's own register (F-193 to F-213) and journals (Sessions 100-119). It takes from Which Term Yields (Session 113) the scheme, the prompt and the readers, with the one sentence S113.SIDE allowed; and from experiments 8 and 9 the fresh reader as a check on the practice's coding. The operation it bears on is judging, where the project document says the error line meets the project: how this practice decides which term of a difference yields.
material: works/fehlerkataster-063.md to -069.md (F-193 to F-213) and journal entries of Sessions 100-119, this repository (CC BY 4.0)
